o.text: From English radio via Russian ра́дио (rádio).
From Proto-Turkic *tẹr. Cognate with Karakhanid تَرْ (ter), Turkish ter, Chuvash тар (tar), etc.
From Classical Persian مُسَلْمَان (musalmān), from Arabic مُسْلِم (muslim).

From Proto-Turkic *til (“tongue”). The change from front to back vowel predates the earliest written record in the 11th century. Cognate with Turkish dılak, Kazakh тылақ (tılaq). Compare also Kyrgyz тилчик (tilcik).
Borrowed from Classical Persian لابد (lābud), from Arabic لَا بُدَّ (lā budda).
